state.package_evidence: The first incremental audit rejected stale packaged manifest metadata even though CODE/DATA bytes matched. Canonical linux-firmware Makefile now declares all three staged files in PKG_FILE_DEPENDS before package rules. A subsequent world passes exact packaged CODE/DATA/manifest validation. Another world with unchanged source and a fresh stage also passes exact packaged-to-staged manifest validation. Both are offline FIT/board/package/module inspections, not router boot.
state.loader_evidence: Actual Linux C passes parser/publication fault tests and uses get_random_bytes_wait before the exposure latch/copies. Actual C-published bytes feed native instruction emulation with kernel/RNG/I/O and native IRQ/backing dependencies modeled. Full strict RX0/RX2/TXDONE setup is still denied. The host RNG fixture is deterministic; this does not prove physical randomness.
state.lifetime_evidence: Actual C retains exposed coherent mailbox buffers with device/module references after failure/detach. Same-instance reload and retained same-device rebind deny. There is no physical retirement/reclaim implementation. Readback,format flags or software parking do not establish prior-user cold exclusion or DMA drain.
state.current_doc:
The normal experimental image now packages the checked MT7996 CODE/DATA pair.
The actual Linux loader checks its ABI/digests and zero session storage, obtains
a nonzero runtime random identity, publishes the real private memory/request
plan and identity, and checks SRAM readback. Exposed DMA mailboxes are retained;
same-instance reload and retained-device rebind are rejected. Retirement is not
implemented, so the module remains pinned after exposure.

Actual-C fault/mutant tests, all-hart native boot from C-published bytes, full raw
RX/TXDONE/BA replay, independent assembly, two package builds and incremental
manifest refresh pass. Latest offline-verified FIT: `05ca2802...`; previous images
are preserved. No flash or router contact. Physical cold containment, complete
strict setup, other owners/hot lifecycle, drains/recovery and clients remain open.
The newest entry defines current state; older dated entries retain their original
scope. Details: `research/checkpoints/2026-10-10-npu-loader-publish/REPORT.md`.
